purpose: Close post-D-Day Kwajalein/Roi-Namur combat, test whether the longer ground reduction creates a Japanese re-attack window, close immediate post-capture airfield/logistics/submarine effects, and set—not resolve—the next US/Japanese Central-Pacific schedules before returning to Bengal.

ground_closeout.Roi: Already effectively secured by 6-Feb 18:00; debris clearance and base-party work begin while Namur fighting continues.
ground_closeout.atoll_cleanup: Outer-islet/security/sweep activity continues into 10-11 Feb but no longer requires division-scale assault combat.
ground_closeout.note: Death/wounded split remains reserved for consolidated Allied death tally.

reason: Shokaku/Zuikaku are already withdrawing west after the 3-Feb exchange.
Hiryu is at/approaching Truk repair and cannot provide a third combat deck.
A reversal would face roughly ten surviving US fast decks plus CVE/fire-support forces without a fresh carrier-quality track.
Longer ground fighting fixes US amphibious/support forces geographically but does not recreate the 3-Feb positive-EV mission-split carrier geometry.

land_air.mission: Fixed-target night harassment of Roi airfield/construction/logistics rather than another moving-ship torpedo search.
land_air.source: Surviving/repaired Eniwetok-centered land-attack reserve with one cue/search element; no new squadron spawned.

outcome_center.material_effect: Localized engineer/store/fuel/ammunition-area damage; no runway denial longer than about one day centered.

land_air.upper_branch_guard: A historical-style bomb-dump chain reaction can produce 100+ casualties and larger material loss, but it is not centered.

submarine.centered_result: Remaining boats obtain reports and one poor/medium-quality approach, but no second US ship hit is centered after LST-224.
submarine.Japan_cost: One additional boat mission-damaged or forced into early withdrawal centered; another sinking is sensitivity, not center.
submarine.reason: Target density remains attractive while unloading/support continues, but US CVE/land-air/DD-DE ASW concentration is now at maximum and known submarine corridors are heavily prosecuted.

marshall_air_after_closeout.by_1944-02-10: Roi/Kwajalein aviation nodes are lost. Surviving Japanese Marshall aviation is fragmented among Wotje/Mili/Jaluit/Eniwetok/outer water nodes and is primarily harassment/recon/local defense.
marshall_air_after_closeout.coordinated_strike_capacity: No second mass strike centered after the 8/9-Feb harassment; surviving night-attack crews are preserved or withdrawn west where possible.
marshall_air_after_closeout.Kinsei_forward_order: The late-Jan 6-8 aircraft order remains stopped west of the Marshall battle area; it is not automatically released to Bengal because Truk/Palau/Marianas cover now becomes the next Central-Pacific demand.

Majuro.state: Already secured and functioning as the independent fast-fleet replenishment/logistics node.
Majuro.fast_carrier_rotation_center: First elements 8-Feb; main TF58 replenishment concentration 9-10 Feb.

delay_drivers: construction overlaps with residual Namur fighting, so not all five days propagate
8/9-Feb Japanese harassment adds about one day centered

US_postcapture_activation.Kwajalein_lagoon: By 10-12 Feb it is a secure assault/logistics anchorage, but Majuro remains the better immediate fast-fleet service hub.

US_next_operation_schedule_working.TF58_decks: Cabot remains campaign-out; Intrepid is near-normal from 4-Feb. Ten fast decks are physically available before detachments, subject to aircraft/crew replenishment.

HAILSTONE_equivalent.logic: Historical TF58 required roughly a week between Majuro replenishment and Truk attack. Branch local fighting and 3-Feb carrier losses shift the sortie several days, but Majuro and the CVE/old-BB support split prevent a multi-week delay.
HAILSTONE_equivalent.force_note: A portion of the light-carrier/CVE force can support Eniwetok while the main fast-carrier mass attacks Truk; do not assume all ten fast decks strike Truk.

CATCHPOLE_equivalent.band: Atoll secure about 26-28 Feb if no new major fleet/submarine shock occurs.
CATCHPOLE_equivalent.logic: Most Eniwetok assault troops are not the units finishing Kwajalein, so the extra ground-combat days do not propagate one-for-one. LST-224 loss, support-ship turnaround and longer Kwajalein unloading impose a smaller 3-5 day net shift from historical Catchpole.

carrier_force.Shokaku_Zuikaku: Continue westward preservation after 3-Feb; no Marshall return.
carrier_force.Hiryu: Truk emergency repair 5-15 Feb; limited deck 12-16 Feb; preferred westward evacuation once ferry/recovery safe, around 14-17 Feb, before the centered US Truk window.
carrier_force.Soryu: Separate 5-15 Feb trial/team-readiness gate; not retroactively inserted into Flintlock.
carrier_force.first_line_team_reconstitution: Three-deck-class first-line availability may reappear late Feb, but carrier-air cadre debt persists into March.

Truk.evacuation_trigger: Kwajalein loss + US reconnaissance/contact evidence makes a Truk raid highly probable.
priority: repair ship/mobile repair specialists after Hiryu emergency work
fleet oilers/tenders/high-value reconnaissance and logistics assets
major combatants not needed for local evacuation cover
Truk.destination_logic: Palau/western Carolines/Philippines/home waters rather than re-concentrating the Combined Fleet at Truk.

Japan_next_schedule_working.Marshall_submarines: Remaining local boats transition from close Kwajalein penetration to outer reporting/withdrawal and future Eniwetok approach lanes; repeated close attacks without fresh cue are NO-GO.

strategic_effect_before_return_to_Bengal.Central_Pacific_priority: Remains HIGH through at least the HAILSTONE/CATCHPOLE gate. Flintlock victory does not free Japanese new fighters westward immediately; it shifts the demand from the lost Marshalls to Truk/Palau/Marianas.
strategic_effect_before_return_to_Bengal.Bengal_Kinsei: Existing Chittagong quality detachment remains; the additional 6-8 aircraft previously held for Central Pacific are still not released to Bengal at the 10-Feb closeout.
strategic_effect_before_return_to_Bengal.Bengal_Raiden: A full 18-30-aircraft priority Raiden detachment to Patenga remains a discretionary tradeoff, not an automatic post-Flintlock release. Reconsider only after the Truk/Eniwetok disposition is known or if Eastern Fleet pressure forces a western allocation change.
strategic_effect_before_return_to_Bengal.Bengal_resume_clock: Return to Bengal at approximately 1944-02-10/11 with the next 10-17 days explicitly shadowed by Central-Pacific and Eastern-Fleet schedule gates.

historical_sanity_anchors: Historically Roi/Namur were secured 2-Feb, Roi reconstruction was ordered 5-Feb, and the first fighter squadron operated from Roi on 13-Feb.

Historically Japanese aircraft successfully raided Roi on 12/13-Feb, causing substantial personnel/material damage without destroying the runway, proving a post-capture fixed-target night attack window existed.
Historically fast carriers replenished at Majuro and departed 12/13-Feb for the 17-18-Feb Truk raid while Eniwetok was attacked in parallel.
Historically the Eniwetok expeditionary group sortied from Kwajalein on 15-Feb and the operation ran 17-23 Feb.
Historical timing is used only as a process/turnaround anchor; Branch dates are shifted by the 3-Feb carrier exchange, 6-Feb D-Day, longer ground reduction and LST-224 loss.
next_exact_action: Resume Bengal/Arakan from the late-Jan/early-Feb stalemate clock. Build RAF/IAF fighter OOB and fielding schedule against the Japanese Chittagong/Patenga fighter allocation, while carrying Central-Pacific HAILSTONE/CATCHPOLE and Eastern-Fleet readiness as explicit future gates rather than resolved outcomes.
